input.prompt:
Create ONE complete new illustrated front cover for 'The Vegetable Guru', a sophisticated practical UK gardening book, portrait proportions 185:240 (approximately 1110 x 1440 pixels). This is a fresh design direction to compare with a separately saved photographic cover, not an edit of that photograph and not a reproduction of an existing competing book. A mature professionally art-directed book jacket, warm, confident and legible at thumbnail size. Flat front cover only, no 3D mockup, no spine, no spread or multiple options in one image.

REFERENCE ROLES: images 1–3 are the AUTHORITATIVE APPROVED VEGETABLE ILLUSTRATION STYLE from the book interior. Match their drawing language: bold simplified crop silhouettes, broad overlapping colour and shadow planes, clear sculptural volume, vivid but controlled crop colours, lime/forest foliage, distinctive cream highlight slashes and small rhythmic highlight strips. Leaves use a bold midrib, a few branches and folded planes; root shapes and markings are graphic and confident. Do not simply match colour while changing to fine botanical drawing. Avoid etched veins, stippling, root hairs, fine cross-hatching, soft watercolour modelling, photographic gloss, heavy black outlines, kawaii faces, clip-art tiles or an assortment of unrelated styles. Their displayed dark/transparent surround and glow are NOT part of the artwork style: no dark halos or glows around individual crops. Image 4 is an ACTUAL LILITA ONE TYPE SPECIMEN; copy this font's recognisable letter shapes and friendly sturdy character. Use this ONE family for title, subtitle, author and small text throughout; no retro slab serif, no curls, no second typeface. Compose original lettering cleanly with careful optical spacing, hierarchy and generous breathing room.

Exact main title: 'The Vegetable Guru' with small 'The' and emphatic 'Vegetable' and 'Guru'. Exact subtitle: 'Your at-a-glance growing companion'. Exact author: 'John Lennon'. Also include one small discreet red play symbol with dark or light high-contrast words 'As seen on YouTube' and '@hackriculture', clearly secondary. No other text, labels, guide counts, fake quotes, logos or claims. All text complete and readable inside safe margins. Good deliberate relationships between illustration and type: a few leaves may approach or carefully pass beside/behind a letter edge, but never obscure a word. Do not create a generic template with a floating sticker and disconnected clip-art scattered everywhere. Use ONE coherent artwork composition and a clear title area. No photograph, person, portrait or character mascot. This is a front-cover CONCEPT, not technical gardening instructions.

DESIGN A — HARVEST ON CREAM. Warm ivory paper ground #fff8e9, deep forest-green title #173e2c, with restrained bright crop colours and a little warm ochre/peach. A spacious asymmetric editorial composition. Big title in the upper half, left aligned with 'The' modest, 'Vegetable' on one strong line and 'Guru' beneath, beautifully spaced in the Lilita reference letterforms. A quiet two-line subtitle sits immediately below the title, using the same face at a much smaller size. This is a direct title/subtitle treatment, not a circular subtitle sticker. The lower half is occupied by ONE elegant broad illustrated harvest grouping, carefully arranged with generous irregular pockets of ivory negative space: three carrots with graphic tops running diagonally across the group, a small cluster of red tomatoes, two purple beetroots with leaves and a few green bean pods. It is a composed still life rather than a huge overflowing harvest heap; each crop has scale and breathing room and plants overlap naturally. One or two leaf stems rise beside the bottom of 'Guru', connecting the art to the title. Maybe a very simple pale-peach organic ground shape beneath the group to hold it together, but no enclosing circle, table, crate, busy pattern or tiled background. Rich broad shadow planes and crisp graphic highlights precisely in the approved hero language. Make the vegetables feel sculptural, confident and mature, not childish or hyper-glossy. A clean bottom margin carries 'John Lennon'; small YouTube feature can balance this footer or occupy the quiet top right. Title dominates, then harvest, then useful subtitle. Strong, calm, inviting and unmistakably a vegetable-growing guide.

DESIGN B — A CONNECTED KITCHEN GARDEN ON FOREST GREEN. Rich deep forest-green cover ground approximately #064d32, with an exceptionally clear large WHITE Lilita One title in the upper central half. Small 'The', substantial 'Vegetable' on a single line, and 'Guru' beneath; retain the natural rounded sturdy font without distortion. The subtitle 'Your at-a-glance growing companion' sits in two readable white lines below the title, no circular sticker. Around and below this open title area, design ONE cohesive simplified kitchen-garden illustration: a gently curving light warm soil path leads in from the bottom through two modest growing beds, with graphic carrot foliage, a few beetroot, lettuces, climbing beans on three or four canes and one tomato plant bearing a few red fruits. A small simple greenhouse sits toward the middle-right distance, integrated into the growing scene. Do NOT make dozens of tiny plants, disconnected vegetable icons, a patchwork grid or a generic scenic landscape. Use a close editorial crop and a controlled handful of plant forms, with recognisable larger vegetables/foliage in the foreground. Some broad foliage rises up the left and right edges, naturally framing the title while leaving it entirely readable. The path and leaves should guide the eye through a connected composition. Match the reference heroes' dimensional broad colour planes, strong silhouettes and sparse cream highlight strokes; simplify greenhouse/canes and ground in the same drawing language, with no detailed hatching or naturalistic texture. Crop greens are lime, mid green and forest shadows; red tomatoes and warm orange roots provide a few purposeful accents. This is an illustrated working garden, not a children's storybook or an antique botanical engraving. 'John Lennon' sits clearly at the bottom in white on a calm dark strip integrated with the green ground. Small discreet YouTube play mark and white supporting text near the top right or footer. Strong hierarchy, plenty of dark breathing room around type, coherent and more immersive than the harvest still life.
